walkthroughs.body_html: Vertical farms stack crops in climate-controlled buildings, using LEDs tuned to plant pigments. They save 95 percent of water vs field farming via recirculation, eliminate pesticides and operate year round. Yields per square metre can be 10 times higher for leafy greens. Energy demand is the main constraint, so renewables and waste heat reuse are key.

Hydroponic systems suspend plant roots in nutrient solution or inert media like rockwool. NFT (nutrient film technique) and DWC (deep water culture) are common methods. Hydroponics use less land and water but rely on synthetic nutrients. Aquaponics adds fish whose waste fertilises crops, creating closed nutrient loops.

Regenerative agriculture rebuilds soil through no-till, cover crops, mob grazing, diverse rotations and minimal chemicals. Healthy soil stores more carbon, holds more water and supports more biodiversity. Farms like Knepp in West Sussex have shown how rewilding plus livestock can restore ecosystems while producing food.
